question.problem:
$\,$ $n$ is not divisible by $3$ and $n$ is not divisible by $5.$

What is the negation of the compound statement above?
question.worked_solution:
De Morgan's law posits that the negation of a conjunction of two statements is equivalent to the disjunction of the negated individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows.

$$
¬(A∧B)=¬A∨¬B
$$

So, the negation of our statement is

$$
\begin{aligned}\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,¬(n\text{ is not divisible by }3\text{ and } & n\text{ is not divisible by }5) \\  & ≡¬((n\text{ is not divisible by }3)∧(n\text{ is not divisible by }5)) \\  & ≡¬(n\text{ is not divisible by }3)∨¬(n\text{ is not divisible by }5) \\  & ≡(n\text{ is divisible by }3)∨(n\text{ is divisible by }5) \\  & ≡n\text{ is divisible by }3\text{ or }n\text{ is divisible by }5.\end{aligned}
$$
